followup_reviews.Separate challenger: GPT-6 Astra Pro /root/verification_recovery, separate same-model context
followup_reviews.Research finding: Intentional Kenyan maize import holds are supported at two named crossings. These are distinct from a protest blockade and from Tanzania-bound transit-truck restrictions; retain the included parent. Busia concerns Ugandan maize awaiting Kenya entry. Namanga concerns Kenyan-owned maize from Tanzania; consignments returned to Tanzania are not Kenya-entry releases. Other goods and all-passenger closure are not claimed. P1 retains the dated Busia observation around 23 March 2021; P2 retains the 1 April Namanga spot check. Neither has a verified first denial or release. Do not backdate both to the reported 5 March policy or bridge the observations into a continuous all-frontier ban. Aflatoxin/mycotoxin concerns are the source-attributed food-safety justification. The later minister’s denial of a blanket ban and journalistic farmer/election context remain qualifications, not additional official rationales. Three relevant article bodies were freshly inspected. The Busia Monitor passage was available before a subscription prompt. Earlier challenge involvement is disclosed; fresh access does not create independent human review. Both accepted phases are unlocated pending B01. Named crossing identities support the textual scope, but no coordinates, gate line, or nationwide outline is certified here.
followup_reviews.Challenge verdict: Accepted within the root decision; see frozen challenge

Withdraw the unsupported Beitbridge cargo endpoint and exact Sadao duration, retain the Benapole quarantine, recognise the observed Rumichaca reopening and append the accessible Korala report. Apply the challenger’s medical-visa cohort, shared-reporting inference and unread-translation metadata refinements. Unknown dates, continuity, exceptions, missing source access and geographic limits remain explicit.
